note: 您 is 你 with a heart 心 underneath: 'you, from the heart'. Used to elders, customers and strangers in the north; in the south 你好 is fine for almost everyone.

example.en: Hello, may I ask your surname?

note: 早 shows the sun 日 rising over 十. Friends just say 早! (zǎo), like 'morning!'. 上 after a time word means 'during'.
晚 has the sun 日 beside 免; it means 'late' as well as 'evening'. Unlike English, there is no everyday 'good afternoon' greeting; 下午好 exists but sounds formal.
安 'peace, safe' is a woman 女 under a roof 宀. The apostrophe in wǎn'ān keeps the syllables apart; without it 'wanan' could be read as wa-nan.
客气 'polite, standing on ceremony' is literally 'guest manner'. 不 changes from fourth to second tone before another fourth tone, so it is said bú kèqi.
意思 'meaning, intention'; 不好意思 is 'embarrassed'. The everyday apology for bumping into someone, being a bit late or interrupting. Heavier apologies use 对不起.

example.roman: Bù hǎoyìsi, wǒ lái wǎn le.

note: Opens any polite question to a stranger: 请问，洗手间在哪里？ 问 is a mouth 口 inside a door 门: a mouth at the doorway, asking.

example.en: Excuse me, where is the metro station?

note: 事 'matter, affair'; 没事 (or 没事儿 in Beijing) means 'nothing's wrong, don't worry'. A relaxed reply to apologies and to 'are you okay?'.
好 before an adjective means 'very': 好久 'a very long time'. English 'long time no see' matches it word for word; whether English copied Chinese or a Native American pidgin is debated.
迎 'to go to meet' has the walking radical 辶. Shops greet you with 欢迎光临 (huānyíng guānglín), 'welcome, your light arrives'.
Often doubled: 恭喜恭喜. The New Year greeting 恭喜发财 (gōngxǐ fācái) means 'congratulations and get rich'; Cantonese 'kung hei fat choi' is the same phrase.
快乐 'happy' is literally 'fast and joyful'. The pattern X快乐 covers every holiday: 新年快乐, 圣诞快乐 (Christmas). 乐 is also read yuè, 'music', as in 音乐.
Said both on 1 January and at Chinese New Year (春节, the Spring Festival). 年 was once a drawing of a person carrying grain: a harvest, hence a year.
Literally 'empty the glass', and at a formal dinner people may really drain it. Japanese kanpai 乾杯 uses the same characters. 干 is the simplified form of 乾 (dry).
麻烦 'trouble, hassle' is hemp 麻 plus vexed 烦 (fire 火 by a head 页, a burning head). Softens a request: 麻烦你帮我拿一下 'could you pass me that'.

example.roman: Máfan nǐ zài shuō yí biàn.
example.en: Could you say that once more?

note: Said by a host or shopkeeper as you leave: 'go slowly', i.e. go safely. The same idea gives 慢用 (màn yòng) 'eat slowly' = enjoy your meal.
辛 and 苦 both mean 'bitter'; 辛苦 is 'laborious'. Said to colleagues, drivers, delivery staff: acknowledging effort is a core courtesy. 了 marks the state reached.
打 'to hit' is a very loose verb: 打电话 phone, 打车 hail a taxi, 打扰 disturb. Said when entering someone's office or leaving a visit.
问题 is both 'question' and 'problem'. 没 negates 有 (have): 没有问题 'there is no problem'. Also used to mean 'sure, can do'.
'Guard what is important' or 'keep your weight', said at partings and to someone ill. 保 'protect' shows a person 亻 carrying a child.
高兴 'glad' is 'high spirits'. 认识 is 'to know (a person)', different from 知道 (know a fact). 很 is nearly obligatory before adjectives and often means little.
进 is simplified from 進 (a bird 隹 walking 辶); the simplified form uses 井 'well' only for its sound. 请 + verb makes any polite instruction.
坐 shows two people 人人 sitting on the ground 土. Do not confuse with 座 (seat) or 做 (to do), both also zuò.
A four-character farewell. 一 shifts to second tone before the fourth-tone 路, hence yílù. 平安 'safe and sound' also appears in 平安夜, Christmas Eve.
A loan from English 'bye-bye', written with 拜 'to bow in respect', which fits nicely. Very common among young people and on the phone; 再见 is the neutral form.
Also written with the Arabic figure 0 or the circle 〇, the only round 'character'. 零 originally meant 'drizzle, fragment' (rain radical 雨). In phone numbers it is read líng.
One stroke. Its tone shifts: yī alone, yí before a fourth tone (一个 yí ge), yì before other tones (一天 yì tiān). On tickets and phone numbers it is often read yāo to avoid confusion with 七.
Two strokes. Used when counting, in 十二 (12), 二十 (20), and in ordinals 第二. Before a measure word Chinese switches to 两: 两个人, never 二个人.
The form of 'two' used before measure words and in 两百, 两千, 两万: 两杯茶 'two cups of tea'. Also an old weight unit, the tael, still used in markets (50 g).
Three strokes. 一二三 are the easiest characters in the script; a joke tells of a boy who assumed 'four' was four strokes. 三 also means 'several': 三思 'think three times' = think it over.
Sounds like 死 sǐ 'death', so it is the unlucky number: many buildings skip the 4th floor and phone numbers with 4 are cheaper. The character shows a box with legs inside.
In finger counting 1-5 are shown as in Europe, with an open hand for five. 五 appears in 五星红旗, the five-starred red flag of the PRC.
One-handed finger counting starts here: six is thumb and little finger stretched out. A lucky number meaning 'smooth going', as in the saying 六六大顺.
Hand sign: all fingertips pinched together. Easily confused with 一 on the phone, so one is read yāo. 七月 is July: months are just numbers plus 月.
The luckiest number: bā sounds like 发 fā in 发财 'get rich'. The Beijing Olympics opened on 8/8/2008 at 8:08 pm. Hand sign: thumb and index finger spread, like the shape of 八.
Sounds like 久 jiǔ 'long-lasting', so 99 roses mean eternal love. The emperor's number: the Forbidden City's doors have 9×9 studs. Hand sign: a hooked index finger.
A cross: one horizontal, one vertical. Hand sign: a fist, or two crossed index fingers. 10 to 99 are built by multiplication and addition: 十一 11, 二十 20, 九十九 99.
Teens are 'ten + digit': 十二 12, 十五 15, 十九 19. No irregular forms at all. 十一 also names the 1 October national holiday, 'Golden Week'.
Tens are 'digit + ten': 三十 30, 五十 50. Then add units: 二十五 25. In fast speech 二十 shrinks to 'èi' ('èi kuài' twenty yuan).
Always takes a number: 一百 100, 两百 200. 100 means 'a lot': 百货商店 'hundred-goods shop' = department store, 百姓 'hundred surnames' = the common people.
一千 1,000, 两千 2,000. Contains 十 under a slanted stroke. 千万 'ten million' is also an adverb meaning 'whatever you do': 千万别忘了 'don't you forget'.
Chinese groups digits by four, not three. 100,000 is 十万 'ten ten-thousands', a million is 一百万. 万 (traditional 萬) also means 'myriad': 万岁 'ten thousand years' = long live!

example.roman: Běijīng yǒu liǎng qiān duō wàn rén.
example.en: Beijing has over twenty million people.

note: The next unit after 万: 一亿 = 100,000,000, 十亿 = a billion. 中国有十四亿人 'China has 1.4 billion people'. Traditional 億 has the person radical 亻 next to 意.
Ordinals are simply 第 + number: 第二 second, 第十 tenth. 第 has the bamboo radical, from the bamboo slips once used for ordered records. 第一名 is first place.
一半 'one half'; 半个小时 'half an hour'; 两点半 'half past two'. The character shows an ox 牛 split by a stroke: an ox cut in two.
Every counted noun needs a measure word between number and noun: 三个人 'three people'. 个 is the all-purpose one and usually unstressed (ge). Simplified from 個; 一个 is said yí ge.
A tree 木 with a mark at the root: 'root, origin', as in 日本 Japan 'sun origin'. As a measure word it counts bound volumes: 一本书 a book, 两本词典 two dictionaries.
Wood 木 plus 不: a cup. Counts drinks by the cup or glass: 一杯茶, 三杯啤酒. Many measure words are containers used this way: 碗 bowl, 瓶 bottle, 盘 plate.
Counts most animals and one of a pair: 一只猫 a cat, 两只手 two hands. Simplified 只 merges 隻 (zhī, measure word) and 只 (zhǐ, 'only'), so watch the tone.
A bow 弓 being drawn: 'to spread out'. Counts flat, spread things: 一张纸 a sheet of paper, 一张票 a ticket, 一张床 a bed, 一张桌子 a table. Also a very common surname.

example.roman: Qǐng gěi wǒ yì zhāng piào.

note: 父 (father) over 巴 (the sound). Family words double the syllable, with the second one toneless. Formal 'father' is 父亲 fùqīn; many children say 老爸 'old dad'.
Woman 女 plus 马 'horse' for the sound mā, with a different tone from 马 mǎ. Formal 'mother' is 母亲 mǔqīn. The first-tone mā is the classic textbook tone example.
Chinese always marks whether a sibling is older or younger; there is no plain word for 'brother'. 哥 is also a friendly address for a slightly older man: 王哥, 'Brother Wang'.

example.en: My older brother works in Shanghai.

note: Woman radical 女 plus 且. Also used to address a young woman politely in shops (小姐姐 online). The 'sister' in 空姐 'air hostess'.
兄弟 xiōngdì 'brothers' uses the literary word 兄 for older brother. 弟 also gives 徒弟 'apprentice' and 兄弟 is used among close male friends.
Woman 女 plus 未 'not yet': the one not yet grown. Internet slang 妹子 'girl'. 姐妹 'sisters' is used among close female friends.
Chinese separates the two sides of the family: 爷爷/奶奶 are the father's parents, 外公/外婆 ('outside' grandparents) the mother's. 爷 is also used for respected old men.
奶 also means 'milk' (牛奶): woman radical 女 plus 乃. Children call any elderly woman 奶奶 politely.
外 'outside' because traditionally a married daughter belonged to her husband's family, so her parents were 'outside' relatives. Northern China also says 姥爷 (lǎoye) and 姥姥 (lǎolao).
儿 is the simplified form of 兒, a child with an open skull. The suffix 子 is toneless. The 'r' of 儿 is the famous Beijing retroflex ending, as in 哪儿 nǎr.
The ü vowel is written ǚ after n and l (女 nǚ, 绿 lǜ) because nu and nü are different syllables. The apostrophe separates nǚ from ér.
Measure word: 个. 孩 has the child radical 子 plus 亥. 小孩 (xiǎohái) is 'small child, kid'. 子 alone was the old word for child and now a toneless suffix on many nouns.
丈 is an old length unit (about 3.3 m); the folk reading is 'a man a zhang tall'. In conversation people say 老公 (lǎogōng) for husband and 老婆 (lǎopo) for wife.
妻 is a woman 女 beneath a hand holding her hair, an old marriage image. Formal; everyday speech uses 老婆 'old lady' or 太太 'Mrs'. Measure word: 个 or polite 位.
朋 looks like two moons 月 side by side (originally two strings of shells); 友 shows two hands together. Measure word: 个, polite 位. 好朋友 is a close friend.

example.roman: Tā shì wǒ de hǎo péngyou.

note: Simply 'male friend', but it always means a romantic partner; a male friend who is just a friend is 男性朋友. Often shortened to 男友.
男 is a field 田 over strength 力: the one who works the fields. 女 was a drawing of a kneeling figure. These two characters mark toilet doors: 男 / 女.
Can sound blunt; 女士 (nǚshì, Ms, lady) is the polite public form and 女孩 (nǚhái) is 'girl'. Measure word: 个 or 位.
A pictograph of a walking figure, two legs. Measure word: 个 (or 位 politely). Chinese nouns have no plural: 一个人 one person, 三个人 three people. 中国人 'Chinese person'.
家 is a pig 豕 under a roof 宀: a household with its livestock. 家 also means 'home' and counts businesses (一家饭馆, a restaurant). 'How many in your family?' is 你家有几口人？

example.roman: Wǒ de jiārén dōu zài Běijīng.
example.en: My family are all in Beijing.

note: Originally 'one born earlier', hence teacher or master; Japanese sensei is the same word. Follows the surname: 王先生 Mr Wang. 女士 (nǚshì) is the female counterpart, 'Ms'.
王小姐 'Miss Wang' is standard in Taiwan and Hong Kong. In mainland China it picked up a slang sense of 'escort', so to call a waitress people say 服务员 or 美女 instead.
Strictly the mother's sister, but used for any woman of your parents' age: children say 阿姨好. Also the usual word for a housekeeper or nanny. 阿 is a friendly prefix on names.
Strictly the father's younger brother (his older brother is 伯伯 bóbo), but children call any grown man 叔叔. Chinese has a different word for each kind of uncle and aunt.
'The big household' = everyone. 大家好 'hello everyone' opens any speech or video. 大家 can take 都 'all': 大家都知道 'everyone knows'.

example.roman: Dàjiā hǎo, wǒ jiào Lǐ Míng.
example.en: Hello everyone, my name is Li Ming.

note: 米 is the raw grain (and the rice radical), 饭 'meal' is the cooked food. Measure word: 碗 (bowl). 吃饭 'eat rice' means to have a meal of any kind.

example.en: I'd like a bowl of rice.

note: Measure word: 碗. Simplified 面 covers both 面 'face' and 麵 'flour, noodles', so 面 can mean either. Long noodles on birthdays stand for a long life.
Measure word: 个, or 盘 by the plate. The northern New Year's Eve food: their shape recalls old silver ingots, so eating them invites wealth. 饺 has the food radical 饣.
包 'to wrap' shows a fetus 巳 wrapped in 勹; it also means 'bag' (书包 schoolbag, 钱包 wallet). Measure word: 个. A plain bun with no filling is 馒头 mántou.
A pictograph of a flowing stream; as a radical it is squeezed to 氵 on the left (河, 海, 酒). Measure words: 杯 glass, 瓶 bottle. Hot water 热水 is the default drink in China.
Grass radical 艹 over 人 and 木. English 'tea' came via the Min dialect 'te' and Dutch traders; 'chai' and Russian 'chay' came overland from chá. Measure words: 杯, 壶 (pot).

example.en: Do you drink tea or coffee?

note: A loanword for 'coffee'. Both characters carry the mouth radical 口, which Chinese adds to mark a character used purely for its sound. Measure word: 杯.
啤 was coined for the 'bee' of 'beer' (mouth radical 口 + 卑), then 酒 'alcoholic drink' was added. Measure words: 瓶 bottle, 杯 glass. 青岛啤酒 Tsingtao is the famous brand.
奶 alone is 'milk' or 'breast'; 牛 specifies cow. Measure words: 杯, 瓶, 盒 (carton). Milk tea 奶茶 is a huge drinks culture in Taiwan and the mainland.
蛋 'egg' has the insect radical 虫 at the bottom. Measure word: 个. 鸡 is simplified from 雞 (bird 隹 → 鸟 'bird' on the right). 茶叶蛋, tea eggs, are a street snack.
Meat names are animal + 肉 'flesh': 牛肉 beef, 羊肉 lamb, 鸭肉 duck. 肉 as a radical is written like 月 (moon) in body parts: 脚, 脸, 肚.
牛 is a pictograph of an ox head with horns. 牛肉面 beef noodle soup is a national dish in Taiwan and Lanzhou. Slang 牛 means 'awesome'.
The default meat: on a menu 肉 alone usually means pork. 猪 has the dog/animal radical 犭. Pork prices are watched like an economic indicator in China.
Simplified from 魚, a pictograph with head, scales and tail. Measure word: 条 (long things). Homophone of 余 'surplus', so a whole fish is served at New Year: 年年有余 'surplus every year'.
Grass radical 艹 over 采 'pick'. Means both 'vegetable' (青菜, 蔬菜) and 'a cooked dish' or cuisine: 中国菜 Chinese food, 点菜 order dishes. Measure words: 个 (dish), 棵 (plant).
果 is a tree 木 with fruit on top. Water-fruit: juicy fruit, as opposed to nuts (坚果 'hard fruit'). Measure word: 个 for a piece, 种 for a kind.
Measure word: 个. Apple Inc. is 苹果公司. Giving apples on Christmas Eve 平安夜 is a modern custom, because 苹 sounds like 平 'peace'.
香 'fragrant' is grain 禾 over sweet 甘 (now 日). Measure words: 根 (one banana, a 'stick') or 把 (a bunch). 香港 Hong Kong is 'fragrant harbour'.
豆 'bean' plus 腐 'fermented, curdled'. English 'tofu' came through Japanese tōfu from the Chinese word. Measure word: 块 (piece). 麻婆豆腐 is the Sichuan classic.
Water radical 氵; simplified from 湯. In Japanese the same character 湯 means hot water or a bath, a classic false friend. Measure word: 碗. Soup is often served last in a Chinese meal.
Measure words: 片 (slice), 个 (roll). 面包车 'bread vehicle' is a minivan, because of its loaf-like shape.
A pure sound-loan for 'chocolate'; the characters' meanings are irrelevant. Measure word: 块 (piece), 盒 (box). 黑巧克力 dark chocolate.
Rice radical 米 plus 唐 (the Tang dynasty, for the sound). Means sugar and also candy: 喜糖 'happy sweets' are given out at weddings. 糖醋 'sugar-vinegar' = sweet and sour.
辛 'bitter, pungent' plus 束. Sichuan food is 麻辣, numbing (花椒 peppercorn) and spicy (chili). Asking 辣不辣？ 'is it spicy?' is essential. 辣妹 is 'hot girl'.
Water radical 氵 beside 酉, a drawing of a wine jar. Covers all alcohol: 白酒 báijiǔ 'white spirit', 红酒 red wine, 啤酒 beer. 酒店 'alcohol shop' actually means hotel.
馆 'hall, establishment' with the food radical 饣: 咖啡馆 café, 图书馆 library, 博物馆 museum. Measure word: 家. 饭店 'meal shop' usually means a hotel.
餐 is the formal word for a meal (早餐 breakfast, 西餐 Western food). 厅 'hall' also gives 客厅 living room. Measure word: 家. Slightly more upmarket than 饭馆.
Also 咖啡厅 or, from the chain names, 咖啡店. 星巴克 (Xīngbākè) is Starbucks: 星 'star' translates the meaning and 巴克 copies the sound.
单 'list, sheet, single' (simplified from 單). Also used for a computer menu. 'Can I see the menu?' is 请给我菜单. Many restaurants now use a QR-code menu on the table.

example.roman: Qǐng gěi wǒ kàn yíxià càidān.
example.en: Please let me see the menu.

note: 员 'member, person' ends many job words: 演员 actor, 售货员 shop assistant. To call a waiter you simply call out 服务员! It is not rude.
点 is 'dot, point': you point at dishes on the menu. A verb-object compound, so 了 goes in the middle: 点了菜. 点 also orders drinks: 点一杯咖啡.

example.roman: Wǒmen kěyǐ diǎn cài le ma?

note: From Cantonese 埋单 (màaihdāan, 'close the bill'); Mandarin speakers reinterpreted it as 买 'buy' + 单 'bill'. 结账 (jiézhàng) is the more formal equivalent.
好 + verb = 'good to': 好吃 tasty, 好喝 nice to drink, 好看 good-looking, 好听 nice-sounding, 好玩 fun. The highest praise at a meal is simply 很好吃!
Used for anything drunk: tea, soup, beer. 喝 'drink' has the mouth radical 口; its right side 曷 is shared with 渴 'thirsty' (water radical), a handy pair.
Bamboo radical ⺮ over 快 'fast'. One story says boatmen avoided the old word 箸 (zhù) because it sounded like 住 'stop', and said 快 'quick' instead. Measure word: 双 (pair).

example.roman: Qǐng gěi wǒ yì shuāng kuàizi.
example.en: Please give me a pair of chopsticks.

note: Stone radical 石 (pottery) beside 宛. Both a noun and a measure word: 一碗饭 a bowl of rice, 两碗汤 two bowls of soup. 'Rice bowl' 饭碗 is slang for one's job.
Measure word: 个. The suffix 子 makes the noun; bare 杯 is the measure word 'cup of'. 世界杯 is the World Cup, 干杯 'dry the cup' is cheers.
Served free in Chinese restaurants; cold water is seen as bad for the stomach, and 多喝热水 'drink more hot water' is the stock advice for every ailment. 热 has the fire radical 灬.
The ice radical 冫 (two drops of frozen water) beside 水. 加冰 'add ice', 冰水 iced water, 冰淇淋 ice cream. Many Chinese prefer drinks without ice: 不要冰.

example.roman: Yì bēi kělè, bù jiā bīng.

en: to take away (leftovers), to pack up
note: Asking to pack leftovers is normal and not embarrassing: 麻烦打包 'please box this up'. The same word means to pack a suitcase or a software package.
Food sold to be eaten outside. China's delivery apps (美团, 饿了么 'are you hungry') make 叫外卖 'order delivery' an everyday verb. Measure word: 份 (portion).
Meals are time-of-day + 饭: 早饭, 午饭, 晚饭. The formal set uses 餐: 早餐. Typical breakfast: 包子, 豆浆 (soy milk), 油条 (fried dough sticks).
午 is noon (上午 morning 'before noon', 下午 afternoon 'after noon'). Lunch in China is early, often at 12 sharp, followed by a short nap 午睡 in many offices.
Also 晚餐. Chinese dinner is early, around 6 pm, and shared: dishes go in the middle of the table and everyone takes from them with chopsticks.
Food radical 饣 plus 我. 'I'm hungry' is 我饿了, with 了 marking a new state. 饿死了 'starving to death' is the everyday exaggeration.

example.roman: Wǒ è le, wǒmen qù chīfàn ba.
example.en: I'm hungry, let's go and eat.

note: Water radical 氵 plus 曷; compare 喝 'drink' with the mouth radical. 我渴了 'I'm thirsty'. 渴望 'thirst-gaze' means to long for something.
Say it when a host keeps filling your bowl or glass. 够 'sufficient' is 句 beside 多 'much'. Said sharply, 够了！ means 'that's enough!' in an argument.
The pointing phrase that works in every restaurant. 要 'want' is direct but not rude in Chinese. 这个 is often said zhèige in Beijing; 那个 (nàge) is 'that one'.
Tipping is not customary in mainland China; it can even be refused. 费 'fee, expense' has the shell radical 贝 (money), as in 免费 'free of charge'.
Food radical 饣 plus 包 'wrap'. 我吃饱了 'I've eaten my fill' is the polite way to refuse more food. 饱 is the opposite of 饿 and both end in 了 when stated.
旅 shows a banner with people under it, a company on the march. 行 'to go' is also read háng 'row, firm' (银行 bank). 旅游 (lǚyóu) is tourism, 旅行社 a travel agency.

example.roman: Wǒ hěn xǐhuan qù Zhōngguó lǚxíng.
example.en: I really like travelling to China.

note: 护 'protect' plus 照 'shine, certificate' (also 'photo' in 照片). Measure word: 本, like a book. Hotels in China must register every guest's passport.
签 'to sign' (bamboo radical, from bamboo tally slips) + 证 'proof' (speech radical 讠). 办签证 'to apply for a visa'. 免签 is visa-free.
Short for 飞机场 'flying-machine field'. 场 'open ground' also gives 市场 market, 停车场 car park, 广场 square. 首都机场 is Beijing Capital Airport.

example.roman: Qù jīchǎng yào duō cháng shíjiān?
example.en: How long does it take to get to the airport?

note: 火车 'fire vehicle' was coined for the steam locomotive and is still the word for any train. 站 'stand' is 'station, stop'. 北京站 is Beijing Railway Station.
Once a tavern with rooms; now the standard word for a hotel, even an alcohol-free one. 宾馆 (bīnguǎn, 'guest hall') and 饭店 also mean hotel. Measure word: 家.
Measure word: 张 (flat things). 图 'picture, diagram' is simplified from 圖. 高德地图 and 百度地图 are the main map apps; Google Maps does not work in mainland China.
A hand 𠂇 over 工 'work': the left hand holding the tool. 左边 (zuǒbian) 'left side', 往左拐 'turn left'. Chinese traffic drives on the right, Hong Kong on the left.
A hand over a mouth 口: the right hand that feeds you. 右边 'right side', 往右拐 'turn right'. 左右 'left-right' means 'approximately': 十个人左右, about ten people.

example.en: Turn right at the traffic lights.

note: 面 'face, side' makes location words: 前面 front, 后面 back, 上面 top, 下面 bottom, 里面 inside, 外面 outside. 前 also means 'before' in time: 前天 the day before yesterday.
Simplified 后 merges 後 'behind, after' with 后 'empress, queen' (皇后). 后天 is the day after tomorrow, 以后 'afterwards'.
Place it after the landmark: 银行旁边 'next to the bank'. Location words follow the noun in Chinese, the reverse of English. 边 'side' is simplified from 邊.

example.en: The metro station is next to the bank.

note: Traditional 東 is the sun 日 rising behind a tree 木. 东西 'east-west' means 'thing', said to come from the East and West markets of Tang Chang'an. 广东 Guangdong is the 'broad east'.
Originally a bird settling in its nest at sunset. 西方 the West, 西餐 Western food, 西安 Xi'an 'western peace'. Compass points are usually ordered 东南西北 in Chinese.
南方 'the south' means the warmer rice-eating half of China, below the Yangtze. 南京 Nanjing is the 'southern capital'. Homophone of 男 'male' and 难 'difficult'.
Two people standing back to back; the original sense was 'back' (now 背), because one faced south and had the north behind. 北京 is the 'northern capital'.
Walking radical 辶 plus 元. 离这儿远吗？ 'is it far from here?' uses 离 'distance from'. 远方 'far place', 永远 'forever' (eternally far).

example.roman: Jīchǎng lí shì zhōngxīn hěn yuǎn.
example.en: The airport is far from the city centre.

note: Walking radical 辶 plus 斤 'axe' (for the sound). 很近 'very close', 附近 'nearby': 附近有银行吗？ 'is there a bank nearby?'. 最近 'most near' means 'recently'.
一直 'straight on, continuously' + 走 'go'. 一 is yì here, before the second-tone 直. A giver of directions will add 然后 'then' and 往左拐 / 往右拐.

example.roman: Yìzhí zǒu, ránhòu wǎng zuǒ guǎi.
example.en: Go straight on, then turn left.

note: Hand radical 扌; also means 'crutch' and 'kidnap'. 往左拐 / 往右拐 'turn left / right'; 转 (zhuǎn) is a synonym. 拐弯 'turn a bend'.
至 'reach' plus the knife radical 刂 for the sound. Also a result ending: 买到 'manage to buy', 看到 'see', 找到 'find'. 到了！ 'we're here!'. 从...到... is 'from ... to ...'.

example.en: What time does the train arrive in Beijing?

note: 洗手间 'hand-washing room' is the polite word; 厕所 (cèsuǒ) is blunter, 卫生间 'hygiene room' is on signs. 在哪儿 (Beijing) = 在哪里 (south) 'where at'.
Measure word: 张. 火车票 train ticket, 机票 plane ticket, 门票 entrance ticket. 买票 'buy a ticket'. 票 also means 'vote' (投票) and 'banknote' (钞票).
Measure word: 件. 行 'to travel'; 李 is 'plum' and a surname, used here only for the sound (an old spelling 行理). 行李箱 is a suitcase, 托运 to check bags in.
迷 'confused' (walking radical 辶 + 米) + 路 'road'. 我迷路了 'I'm lost'. 迷 also means 'fan': 球迷 football fan, 歌迷 music fan.
Named for the steam engine. 车 is simplified from 車, a cart seen from above with its axle. Measure word: 辆 for vehicles, but trains are counted with 列 or 趟 (trips). 坐火车 'go by train'.
汽 'vapour, steam' (water radical). Measure word: 辆. 开车 'drive', 车 alone is enough in context. Japanese 汽車 means train, a false friend.
公共 'public, shared' (公共厕所 public toilet). Usually shortened to 公交车 (gōngjiāochē) or 公交. 路 numbers bus lines: 3路车 'the number 3 bus'.

example.target: 我每天坐公共汽车上班。
example.roman: Wǒ měitiān zuò gōnggòng qìchē shàngbān.
example.en: I take the bus to work every day.

note: 'Vehicle for hire'. In the south and Hong Kong 的士 (dīshì), a Cantonese loan of 'taxi', is common, and 打的 'hail a taxi' comes from it. Ride-hailing uses 滴滴 (Didi).
Short for 地下铁路 'underground iron road'. 铁 'iron' has the metal radical 钅. Chinese cities have built the world's longest metro networks; Shanghai's is the biggest.

example.en: It's faster to go by metro.

note: Measure word: 辆. 单车 (dānchē, 'single vehicle') is the southern word, now nationwide via 共享单车 'shared bikes'. You 骑 'ride' a bike, not 坐 'sit'.
Measure word: 架. 飞 is simplified from 飛, a bird with spread wings. 机 'machine' appears in 手机 mobile phone ('hand machine') and 机场 airport.
Boat radical 舟 on the left, a pictograph of a hull. Measure word: 条 or 艘. 坐船 'go by boat'. 飞船 is a spaceship.
Short for 高速铁路 'high-speed railway'. China's network, built since 2008, is by far the world's largest, with trains at 350 km/h. Tickets are tied to your passport number.
Any station or stop: 火车站, 公交车站, 地铁站. 站 as a verb means 'to stand'. 下一站 'next stop' is the announcement you will hear on every metro.
Stand radical 立. Counts stops: 坐三站 'ride three stops'. 网站 'net station' is a website, 加油站 a petrol station. As a verb: 站起来 'stand up'.
Two people 人人 on the earth 土. Used for riding any vehicle you sit in: 坐车, 坐飞机, 坐地铁. Bikes and horses take 骑. 请坐 'please sit'.

example.en: Have you ever taken the high-speed train?

note: 开 'open' (simplified from 開, hands lifting a bar from a gate 門) means 'operate': 开车 drive, 开灯 switch on a light, 开会 hold a meeting. Verb-object: 开了车.
Horse radical 马 plus 奇: originally to ride a horse, now also bikes and motorbikes, anything you straddle. 骑自行车 'ride a bike'. Compare 坐 for vehicles you sit inside.
Foot radical 足 plus 各. Measure word: 条. Street names: 南京路 Nanjing Road. 路口 'road mouth' is an intersection; 走路 is to walk. 一路平安 'safe journey'.
行 'go' split around 圭: a thoroughfare. Measure word: 条. 逛街 (guàngjiē) 'stroll the streets' means going shopping for fun. 王府井大街 is Beijing's famous shopping street.
Named after the two colours. 灯 'lamp' has the fire radical 火. Directions often use it as a landmark: 在第二个红绿灯左拐 'turn left at the second set of lights'.
司 'to be in charge of' (as in 公司 company). Used for taxi and bus drivers; address one as 师傅 (shīfu, 'master'), the polite all-purpose title for skilled workers.
堵 'to block up' with the earth radical 土. 堵车了 'we're stuck in traffic', a daily excuse in Beijing. Also 塞车 (sāichē) in the south and Taiwan.
Person radical 亻 plus 亭 'pavilion', a place to halt. 停车 'park a car', 停车场 car park, 不停 'nonstop'. 雨停了 'the rain has stopped'.
打 'hit' used for 'get hold of', as in 打电话 'make a phone call'. 打车 covers street taxis and ride-hailing apps alike. 打的 (dǎdī) is the older slang form.

example.target: 太晚了，我们打车回家吧。
example.roman: Tài wǎn le, wǒmen dǎchē huí jiā ba.
example.en: It's late, let's take a taxi home.

note: 上 'up, onto' and 下 'down, off' pair for boarding: 上车 / 下车, 上飞机 / 下飞机. The same pair gives 上班 'go to work' and 下班 'finish work'.
下 'down' is a line below the baseline, the mirror of 上. 我在下一站下车 'I get off at the next stop'. 下 also means 'next': 下个月 next month.

example.en: Excuse me, are you getting off?

note: The literal home of 加油 'add oil', the cheer. 油 'oil' (water radical) covers petrol and cooking oil alike: 汽油 petrol, 酱油 soy sauce.

en: to walk, to go on foot
note: 走 was originally 'run' (a figure with swinging arms over a foot 止); in modern Mandarin it is 'walk, go, leave'. 走路去 'go on foot'. 走 is also the radical of 起 and 超.
天 'sky, heaven, day' is a big person 大 with a line for the sky above. Days: 今天 today, 明天 tomorrow, 昨天 yesterday, 后天 the day after tomorrow, 前天 the day before.
明 'bright' is the sun 日 next to the moon 月, one of the classic character-building examples. 明年 is next year, 明白 'bright-white' = to understand.
昨 has the sun radical 日, like most time characters (时, 早, 晚, 明). No tense is needed on the verb: 昨天我去了 'yesterday I went', the time word does the work.
现 'appear, present' (simplified from 現, jade 王 + 见 see). 现在几点？ 'what time is it now?'. 现金 'present gold' is cash.
The seven-day week came to China with the Western calendar; the name recalls the seven 'stars' (sun, moon, five planets). 周 (zhōu) and 礼拜 (lǐbài, 'worship') are synonyms. Measure word: 个.
Weekdays are numbered: 星期一 Monday to 星期六 Saturday. Monday is day one because Sunday is the week's 'day' (星期天) or 'sun' (星期日). Also 周一.

example.en: I have to work on Monday.

note: The only day with a name instead of a number; 星期日 is the formal form, 周日 the short one. Note 星期几？ 'which day is it?' uses 几 in the number slot.
A crescent moon pictograph. Months are just numbers + 月: 一月 January, 十二月 December. 月饼 'moon cakes' are eaten at the Mid-Autumn Festival. Measure word: 个 (三个月).
No month has its own name: 二月 February, 三月 March ... 十二月 December. Careful: 一个月 is 'one month' (a duration), 一月 is 'January'. Dates run year-month-day: 2024年1月5日.

Years are read digit by digit: 2024年 = 二零二四年. No measure word is needed: 三年 'three years'. 过年 'pass the year' is to celebrate Chinese New Year; 年 was also a legendary monster scared off by firecrackers.
Measure word: 个 (两个小时 two hours). The old Chinese 时辰 was a two-hour period, so the Western hour became the 'small hour'. 半个小时 half an hour.
分 'divide, fraction' (a knife 刀 cutting 八 apart) + 钟 'clock'. 十分钟 'ten minutes'. In telling time, 分 alone: 三点十分 3:10. 分 is also a cent of money.
三点 3 o'clock, 三点半 3:30, 三点一刻 3:15 (刻 'a quarter'). 几点？ 'what time?'. 点 'dot, point' also orders food (点菜) and means 'a bit' (一点儿).
The early morning, up to about 9; 上午 ('before noon') covers the whole morning. Time words go before the verb: 我早上跑步 'I run in the morning'.
午 'noon' was the seventh earthly branch, the hour of the horse (11-1). 上午 'above noon' is the morning, 中午 'middle noon' is midday. 下午茶 is afternoon tea.
From dusk until bedtime; deep night is 夜里 or 半夜 'half night'. 晚上好 'good evening', 晚饭 dinner, 晚会 an evening party or gala.
周 'cycle, week' + 末 'end' (a tree 木 with a mark at its tip, the opposite of 本 'root'). 周末快乐！ 'have a nice weekend'. 周 is also a very common surname.
生 'to be born, life' is a plant sprouting from the ground. 你的生日是几月几号？ 'what date is your birthday?'. Long-life noodles 长寿面 are the traditional birthday food.
时 is simplified from 時 (sun 日 + 寺); 间 'between, interval' is a sun in a doorway. 有时间吗？ 'do you have time?'. 时候 means 'the time when': 小时候 'in childhood'.
几 'how many' replaces the number: 几点 what time, 几月几号 what date, 星期几 what day. 现在几点了？ 'what time is it now?'. The answer: 两点 (not 二点) for 2 o'clock.
每 'each' is a 母 'mother' with a sprout on top. 每 + time word: 每年 every year, 每个星期 every week. Often paired with 都 'all': 我每天都喝茶 'I drink tea every day'.
Chinese puts the past in front: 前 'front' = before, 后 'back' = after. 以前 can stand alone ('formerly') or follow a clause: 吃饭以前 'before eating'.
The mirror of 以前. 下班以后 'after work', 以后再说 'let's talk about it later'. For 'later today' people say 一会儿 (yíhuìr) 'in a moment'.
Dates in speech: 五月一号 1 May; in writing 日 replaces 号. 号 'number' also gives 号码 (phone number), 几号 'what date', and sizes: 大号 large.
Falls on the first day of the lunar calendar, between late January and mid-February. 节 'festival, joint' has the bamboo radical, from bamboo nodes. Hundreds of millions travel home: the 春运.
颜 'face, countenance' (head radical 页) + 色 'colour'. Colour words usually add 色: 红色, 蓝色. 什么颜色？ 'what colour?'. 色 alone can also mean 'lust' (色狼 a lecher).
Silk radical 纟 (dyed silk) + 工. The colour of luck and joy: weddings, New Year, and 红包 red envelopes of money. 红茶 'red tea' is what English calls black tea. 网红 'net-red' = influencer.
The imperial colour, once reserved for the emperor's robes. 黄河 the Yellow River, 黄帝 the Yellow Emperor. Careful: 黄色 also means 'pornographic' (黄色电影).
Grass radical 艹: originally the indigo plant. 蓝天 blue sky, 蓝色 blue. 青出于蓝 'green comes from indigo' means the student surpasses the teacher.
Silk radical 纟. The ü is written with dots after l (lǜ) because lu is a different syllable. Never give a man a green hat: 戴绿帽子 means his wife is cheating on him. 绿茶 green tea.
Traditionally the colour of mourning, worn at funerals. 白天 daytime, 白酒 clear spirit, 明白 'understand'. 白 also means 'in vain': 白跑一趟 'a wasted trip'.
A chimney blackened by fire 灬 at the bottom. 黑板 blackboard, 黑客 (hēikè) 'black guest' = hacker, a sound-loan. 黑车 is an unlicensed taxi.
Silk radical 糸 under 此. 紫禁城 the Forbidden City is the 'purple forbidden city', after the purple star (Polaris) that stood for the emperor.
粉 'powder' (rice radical 米) + 红. Also simply 粉色. 粉丝 'powder threads' (glass noodles) doubles as a sound-loan for 'fans' of a celebrity.
Named after the fruit 橙 (tree radical 木), just as in English. 橘色 (júsè, tangerine) is also used. The fruit itself is 橙子.
A hand over fire 火: ash you can hold. 灰色 grey, 灰尘 dust. The 'grey' area in 灰色收入 'grey income' is money earned off the books.
After 棕, the palm whose fibre is brown. Many speakers say 咖啡色 'coffee colour' instead. Brown is a late addition to the Chinese colour set.
The old word covering green and blue: 青山 green hills, 青天 blue sky, 青菜 greens. Also 'youth': 青年 young people. 青岛 Qingdao is 'green island'; the beer spells it Tsingtao.
Metal radical, as 钅 in 铁 iron, 银 silver, 钱 money. 金色 golden, 现金 cash, 奖金 bonus. 金 is a common surname (Kim in Korean, Jin in Chinese).
Metal radical 钅 + 艮. 银色 silver (colour), 银行 'silver store' = bank, from the days when silver ingots were money. 银河 'silver river' is the Milky Way.
Water radical 氵: deep water. Dark shades are 'deep': 深蓝 dark blue, 深绿 dark green. Also 'profound': 深刻 'deep carving' = profound.
Water radical: shallow water. Pale shades: 浅蓝 light blue, 浅色 a light colour. 浅 and 深 are the pair for shades, not 轻 'light in weight'.
形 'form' has the 彡 'hair/pattern' radical. 什么形状？ 'what shape?'. Geometric shapes end in 形: 圆形 circle, 方形 square, 三角形 triangle.
A frame 囗 around 员. 圆形 circle; 圆圆的月亮 'the round moon'. The currency yuan 元 was originally 圆 'round', for the round silver dollar; the Japanese yen 円 is the same word.
方形 square shape, 方块字 'square-block characters' is a nickname for Chinese writing. Also 'direction, side': 东方 the East, 地方 place, 方法 method.
角 'horn, corner, angle' is also a tenth of a yuan (one 角 = 10 分). 三角 'triangle' shows up in 三角恋 'love triangle'.
长 is read cháng 'long' here, but zhǎng 'grow, chief' in 长大 'grow up' and 校长 'headmaster'. The same character, two readings: context decides.
Silk radical 纟: a thread. Measure word: 条. 地铁一号线 'metro line 1', 路线 route, 在线 'on the line' = online, 无线 wireless.

example.roman: Zuò èr hào xiàn dào Rénmín Guǎngchǎng.

note: Jade radical 王 + 求. Measure word: 个. 足球 football, 篮球 basketball, 乒乓球 ping-pong (the name is onomatopoeic, borrowed into English). 地球 'earth ball' is the planet.
彩 (彡 pattern radical + 采) means 'bright colours' and 'lottery'. 彩色电视 colour TV, 彩虹 rainbow, 彩票 lottery ticket. 黑白 is 'black and white'.
身 is a pregnant figure in profile; 体 (simplified from 體) is a person 亻 at their root 本. 你身体好吗？ 'how is your health?' is a standard question to elders.
Simplified from 頭 (head radical 页). 头发 hair, 头疼 headache. Also a measure word for cattle (一头牛) and 'first': 头一次 the first time.
Both characters have the eye radical 目, itself a pictograph of an eye turned sideways. Measure word: 只 for one, 双 for the pair. 眼镜 (yǎnjìng) 'eye mirrors' are glasses, a near-homophone.
耳 is a pictograph of an ear and the radical in 听 'listen' (traditional 聽) and 聪 'clever'. Measure word: 只 / 双. 耳机 'ear machine' are headphones.
The top part 自 was originally a drawing of a nose; it came to mean 'self' because Chinese point to their nose when saying 'me'. A new character 鼻 was then made for the nose itself.
The everyday word; 口 (kǒu), a pictograph of an open mouth, is the formal one and the radical of 吃, 喝, 叫, 吗. 嘴巴 is also common. 闭嘴 'shut your mouth'.
A pictograph of a hand with spread fingers; as a radical it becomes 扌 (打, 拿, 找). Measure word: 只 / 双. 手机 'hand machine' = mobile phone, 洗手 wash hands, 握手 shake hands.
Flesh radical 月 (a squashed 肉) marks most body parts. Measure word: 只 / 双. 脚 is the foot; 腿 the leg. 足 is the older word, kept in 足球 football.
Flesh radical 月 + 退 'retreat'. Measure word: 条. 大腿 thigh, 小腿 calf, 鸡腿 drumstick. 腿疼 'my leg hurts'.
Flesh radical 月 + 土. 肚子饿 'belly hungry', 肚子疼 stomach-ache, 拉肚子 'pull belly' = diarrhoea. Read dǔ, 肚 is tripe on a menu.
A pictograph of a heart with its chambers. The radical of feeling words, as 心 (想, 您, 忘) or 忄 (快, 忙, 怕). Measure word: 颗. 心脏 the organ, 小心 careful, 开心 happy.
'Keep your heart small', i.e. attentive. Seen on signs everywhere: 小心地滑 'careful, slippery floor', 小心碰头 'mind your head'. As a verb: 小心点儿 'take a bit more care'.
医 is simplified from 醫 (arrows in a box over a wine jar, the old medicine). Measure word: 个 or 位. Patients address a doctor as 大夫 (dàifu), an old official title. 看医生 'see a doctor'.
院 'courtyard, institution' also gives 学院 college and 电影院 cinema. Measure word: 家. Chinese hospitals combine GP and specialist care, so a cold may mean a hospital visit.
The sickness radical 疒 shows a person lying on a bed; it starts 疼 pain, 瘦 thin, 疫 epidemic. 病人 patient, 看病 'see (about) an illness' = see a doctor.
生 'produce' + 病. 他生病了 'he's ill'. A verb-object compound: 生了病, 生过病. 病 alone also works as a verb: 他病了.

example.target: 他昨天生病了，没来上班。
example.roman: Tā zuótiān shēngbìng le, méi lái shàngbān.
example.en: He got sick yesterday and didn't come to work.

en: a cold; to catch a cold
note: Both noun and verb: 我感冒了 'I've caught a cold'. 冒 'to emit, brave' as in 冒险 'adventure'. Standard advice: 多喝热水 'drink more hot water'.
烧 'burn' has the fire radical 火; also 'cook, roast' (红烧 red-braised). 发 'emit' is simplified from 發 and in 头发 'hair' is a different word, 髮, read fà.
Sickness radical 疒 + 冬 'winter'. Body part + 疼: 头疼 headache, 牙疼 toothache. 痛 (tòng) is the southern synonym. 疼 also means 'to dote on': 疼爱.
Grass radical 艹 over 约: herbal remedies. You 'eat' medicine in Chinese: 吃药. 中药 traditional Chinese medicine, 西药 Western drugs, 药店 pharmacy.

example.roman: Yì tiān chī sān cì yào.
example.en: Take the medicine three times a day.

note: 健 'strong' (person radical 亻 + 建 'build'); 康 'well-being'. 祝你健康 'wishing you good health' is a toast. 健身 'strengthen the body' = working out.
A field 田 over silk 糸: toil. 我累了 'I'm tired', 累死了 'dead tired'. Read lěi it means 'accumulate' (积累), another two-reading character.
休 is a person 亻 leaning against a tree 木, one of the clearest picture-compounds. 息 'breath' is nose 自 over heart 心. 休息一下 'take a short break'.
睡 has the eye radical 目 drooping 垂. 觉 is jiào 'sleep' here, but jué 'feel' in 觉得. Verb-object compound: 睡了觉, 睡个好觉 'sleep well'. 午睡 is the midday nap.

example.en: I go to bed at eleven every day.

note: A pictograph of interlocking teeth. Measure word: 颗. 刷牙 brush teeth, 牙医 dentist, 牙疼 toothache. 牙 also names Spain and Portugal in 西班牙 and 葡萄牙 by sound.
A pig 豕 under a roof 宀: in ancient China a household kept its pig indoors. 回家 'go home', 在家 'at home'. Also a measure word for businesses (一家公司) and a suffix for experts: 画家 painter.
房 is a door 户 over 方. Measure word: 套 (a set, for flats) or 栋 (a building). 买房子 'buy a home' is the great middle-class ambition; 房价 'house prices' is a constant topic.
间 'space between' (sun 日 in a doorway 门) is also the measure word for rooms: 一间房间, 两间卧室. 房间号 is a hotel room number.
Simplified from 門, a drawing of a double-leafed gate. Measure word: 扇. The radical of 问 ask, 间 between, 闻 hear/smell. 门口 'door mouth' is the doorway, 开门 open the door.
窗 has the cave/hole radical 穴 on top. 户 'door, household' is toneless here. Measure word: 扇. 开窗 open the window. 窗口 is a ticket window or counter.
Tree radical 木 at the bottom, like most furniture (椅, 床, 柜). Measure word: 张 (flat surfaces). 桌子上 'on the table': the location word comes after the noun.

example.en: The book is on the table.

note: Tree radical 木 + 奇. Measure word: 把, used for things you grip by a handle or back (椅子, 伞 umbrella, 刀 knife). 轮椅 'wheel chair' is a wheelchair.
Wood 木 under a shelter 广. Measure word: 张. 起床 'rise from bed' = get up, 上床 go to bed, 床单 sheet. Li Bai's most famous poem begins 床前明月光 'moonlight before my bed'.
厨 'kitchen, cook' (also in 厨师 chef) + 房. Chinese kitchens are often small and closed off because stir-frying produces smoke; the wok 锅 is the central tool.
卫生 'guard life' = hygiene, also in 卫生纸 toilet paper. The polite word on signs and in homes; 洗手间 'hand-washing room' in restaurants, 厕所 the plain word.
The room where guests 客 are received. 客 appears in 客人 guest, 客气 polite ('guest manner'), 顾客 customer, 博客 blog (a sound-loan).
A pure sound-loan from English 'sofa' (via Shanghai dialect, where 发 sounds closer to 'fa'). The characters mean nothing here. Measure word: 个 or 套 (a suite).
电 'electricity' (originally 'lightning', simplified from 電 with the rain radical) starts most modern tech words: 电视 TV, 电话 telephone, 电影 'electric shadow' film. Measure word: 台.

example.en: I like watching TV in the evening.

note: 脑 'brain' has the flesh radical 月. Coined in Taiwan and now standard everywhere; the formal term 计算机 'calculating machine' is used in academia. Measure word: 台. 笔记本电脑 laptop.
Measure word: 部 or 个. 手机号 phone number. Everything in China runs through the phone: payment, tickets, menus. 玩手机 'play with the phone' = scroll.

example.roman: Nǐ de shǒujī hào shì duōshao?

note: Fire radical 火 + 丁; simplified from 燈. Measure word: 盏. 开灯 / 关灯 'switch the light on / off' use 'open / close'. 灯笼 is a paper lantern, 红绿灯 traffic lights.
Metal radical 钅 in 钥; 匙 (toneless here) is also 'spoon' (汤匙). Measure word: 把. 钥匙 is a key for a lock; a keyboard key is 键 and a solution's key is 关键.
Person radical 亻 + 主 'master'. 你住在哪儿？ 'where do you live?'. Also a result ending meaning 'firmly': 记住 remember, 站住 halt. Not to be confused with 祝 'wish', same sound.
做 'to make, do' + 饭 'meal'. A verb-object compound: 做了饭, 做过饭. 他做饭很好吃 'he cooks well'. 菜 'dishes' can replace 饭: 做菜.
扫 'sweep' has the hand radical 扌 and gives 扫码 'scan a code'. Homes are cleaned top to bottom before Chinese New Year to sweep out the old year's bad luck.
Both characters carry the water radical 氵. A verb-object compound: 洗了澡, 洗个澡 'take a shower'. 洗 alone is 'wash': 洗手, 洗衣服, 洗碗.
起 'rise' (walk radical 走 + 己) + 床 'bed'. 你几点起床？ 'what time do you get up?'. Verb-object: 起了床. 早起 is 'to rise early'.

example.en: I get up at seven every day.

note: 箱 'box, chest' (bamboo radical ⺮) also gives 行李箱 suitcase and 邮箱 mailbox / email inbox. Measure word: 台 for appliances.
Tree radical 木. 二楼 'second floor' counts the ground floor as 一楼, American style. 楼上 upstairs, 楼下 downstairs, 大楼 a tall building. Floor 4 is often missing because 四 sounds like 'death'.

example.en: My home is on the fifth floor.

note: 邻 has the city radical 阝 on the right; 居 'to dwell' is a body 尸 over 古. Measure word: 个. The saying 远亲不如近邻: a near neighbour beats a distant relative.
衣 is a pictograph of a robe with sleeves and is the radical 衤 in 衬衫, 裤, 裙, 袜. Measure word: 件 (件 counts items and matters). 穿衣服 put on clothes, 买衣服 buy clothes.

en: to wear, to put on (clothes, shoes)
note: A hole 穴 with a tooth 牙: to pierce, pass through. Used for anything the body goes into: clothes, trousers, shoes, socks. Hats, glasses and jewellery take 戴 instead.

example.roman: Jīntiān hěn lěng, duō chuān yìdiǎn.
example.en: It's cold today, wear a bit more.

note: For things attached to the body rather than put on it: 戴帽子 hat, 戴眼镜 glasses, 戴手表 watch, 戴口罩 face mask. Same sound as 带 'bring, carry', a frequent confusion.
Clothing radical 衤 + 库. Measure word: 条 (long things). 一条裤子 is one pair of trousers; there is no 'pair' because Chinese sees one long item. 短裤 shorts, 牛仔裤 jeans.
Clothing radical 衤 + 君. Measure word: 条. A dress is 连衣裙 'joined-garment skirt'. 裙 appears in 围裙 apron.
Leather radical 革 on the left. Measure word: 双 for a pair, 只 for one shoe. 皮鞋 leather shoes, 运动鞋 trainers. Giving shoes as a gift is unlucky: 鞋 sounds like 邪 'evil'.

example.en: How much is this pair of shoes?

note: Clothing radical 衤 + 末. Measure word: 双 / 只. Simplified from 襪. Socks worn with sandals are, as everywhere, a matter of debate.
Cloth radical 巾 + 冒. Measure word: 顶 'top'. Worn with 戴, not 穿. 绿帽子 'green hat' means being cheated on, so green hats never sell in China.
Both characters have the clothing radical 衤. Measure word: 件. 白衬衫 a white shirt. 衫 also appears in 汗衫 'sweat shirt' (a vest) and T恤衫.
A rare word written with a Latin letter. 恤 was chosen in Cantonese, where it sounds like 'shirt'; Mandarin kept the spelling. Also 体恤 or 短袖 'short sleeve'. Measure word: 件.
套 'cover, set' is also the measure word for sets and flats. Measure word for a coat: 件. 大衣 is a long overcoat, 羽绒服 'feather-down clothing' a puffer jacket.
毛 means hair, fur or wool (a pictograph of tufts), and is the surname of Mao Zedong. Measure word: 件. 羊毛 is sheep's wool, 毛巾 a towel.
内 'inside' is 人 entering 冂. The opposite pair 内/外 inside/outside also gives 内容 content and 国内 domestic. Measure word: 件.
镜 'mirror, lens' has the metal radical 钅 from bronze mirrors. Measure word: 副 (a set). Differs from 眼睛 'eyes' only by the tone of the second syllable: jìng vs jing. 太阳镜 sunglasses.
表 'meter, gauge, table' also means a form (表格) and 'to express'. Measure word: 块 or 只. Never give a clock (钟) as a gift: 送钟 sounds like 送终, attending a deathbed. Watches are fine.
Measure word: 个. 书包 schoolbag, 钱包 wallet, 背包 backpack, 包包 handbag (colloquial). The same 包 is in 包子 steamed bun and 红包 red envelope.
Pairing two opposites makes an abstract noun: 大小 size, 长短 length, 多少 quantity, 买卖 trade. In a shop ask 有大一点的吗？ 'do you have a bigger one?'. Sizes use 号: 大号 L, 中号 M.
The 'gown of the Banner people', the Manchu ruling class of the Qing dynasty. Its slim 1920s Shanghai form became the iconic Chinese dress. English 'cheongsam' is the Cantonese name 长衫 'long shirt'.
牛仔 'ox-boy' is a cowboy, so jeans are 'cowboy trousers'. Measure word: 条. The Hong Kong-origin word spread with Western films.
围 'to surround' (a frame 囗 around 韦) + 巾 'cloth', the radical of 帽 hat and 帮 help. Measure word: 条. Worn with 戴 or 围.
Speech radical 讠 + 式. 试一下 or 试试 'have a try', 可以试一下吗？ 'can I try it on?'. 试衣间 is the fitting room, 考试 an exam ('examine-test').
合 'to join' (a lid on a mouth) + 适 'suit'. 很合适 'it fits well / suits you'. 不合适 is the polite way to say something is wrong: a size, a plan, a partner.

example.roman: Zhè jiàn yīfu hěn héshì nǐ.

note: 短 'short' (arrow 矢 + 豆) is the opposite of 长 cháng. Measure word: 条. 短信 'short letter' is a text message, 短裙 a short skirt.
Flesh radical 月 + 兑: to shed from the body. The opposite of 穿: 脱鞋 take off shoes (expected at the door in most Chinese homes), 脱衣服 undress. Hats and glasses use 摘.
丝 (simplified from 絲, two skeins) is the silk radical 纟 in 红, 绿, 线. The English word 'silk' descends, via Latin sericum, from 丝. 丝绸之路 is the Silk Road.
工 is a pictograph of a carpenter's square and means 'work, craft'. Noun and verb: 找工作 look for a job, 我在银行工作 'I work at a bank'. 工人 worker, 工资 wages.
学 (simplified from 學) shows hands over a child 子; 习 (from 習) was a bird's wings 羽, practising flight. Confucius' Analects opens 学而时习之 'learn and practise in due time'.

example.roman: Wǒ xuéxí Zhōngwén liǎng nián le.
example.en: I've been studying Chinese for two years.

note: 校 (tree radical 木) is read xiào 'school' here but jiào 'proofread' elsewhere. Measure word: 所 or 个. 小学 primary, 中学 secondary, 大学 university. 校长 is the head teacher.
生 here is a person suffix, as in 医生 doctor and 先生 Mr. Measure word: 个 or 位. 留学生 'stay-abroad student' is an international student. 学生证 student card.
老 'old' shows respect rather than age, as in 老板 boss, 老婆 wife. 师 'master' (简体 from 師). Address teachers surname + 老师: 王老师. Also a polite title for any expert.
Also the title of a Confucian classic, 'The Great Learning'. 北京大学 (北大) and 清华大学 are the top two. 上大学 'go to university', 大学生 a university student.
Measure word: 家. 公 'public' + 司 'to manage'. 有限公司 is 'Ltd'. The word spread from Chinese merchant partnerships (kongsi) across Southeast Asia in the 18th century.
板 'plank' (wood radical) is used only for the sound. Measure word: 个 / 位. Shoppers call any shop or stall owner 老板, and female owners 老板娘 (lǎobǎnniáng).
同 'same, together' + 事 'matter, work'. Pattern: 同学 classmate ('same study'), 同屋 roommate, 同胞 compatriot. Measure word: 个 / 位.
Also how teachers address students: 同学们 'students!'. A classmate remains a 同学 for life, and 老同学 reunions are a big thing. Measure word: 个 / 位.

en: to go to work, to start work
note: 班 'shift, class, team' (two 王 jade pieces split by a knife). 上班 go on shift, 下班 come off shift, 加班 'add shift' = work overtime, the famous 996 (9 am to 9 pm, 6 days).
你几点下班？ 'when do you get off work?'. 下班以后 'after work'. The 上/下 pair also gives 上课/下课 (class starts / ends) and 上学 go to school.
办公 'handle official business' + 室 'room' (roof radical 宀). 办 'to handle' appears in 办签证 apply for a visa and 办法 'a way to handle it'.
Simplified from 書, a hand holding a brush over writing. Measure word: 本. 看书 'read a book' (literally 'look at'), 书店 bookshop, 图书馆 library. 书法 is calligraphy.
Named after the Han dynasty and the Han ethnic majority. Japanese kanji and Korean hanja are the same word. 字 is a child 子 under a roof 宀: characters 'bred' from simpler ones. Measure word: 个.

example.en: How do you write this character?

note: 中 'middle' from 中国 'Middle Kingdom' + 文 'writing'. Synonyms: 汉语 'Han language', 普通话 'common speech' (Mandarin), 国语 in Taiwan, 华语 in Singapore.
英 is the sound-loan for 'Eng-' in 英国 England/Britain, chosen because it also means 'hero, outstanding'. 语 'language' has the speech radical 讠. 英文 stresses the written language.
考 shows an old man 耂 with a stick; its sense 'examine' comes from the imperial civil-service exams. Noun and verb. 高考 is the university entrance exam, the most stressful day of Chinese youth.
A hand with a stick ⺙ over a child 子 and 爻: instruction, the old-fashioned way. Read jiāo as the verb, jiào in 教育 education and 教室 classroom. Takes two objects: 教我中文 'teach me Chinese'.
Simplified from 寫 (a magpie under a roof, borrowed for the sound). 写字 write characters, 写信 write a letter. Stroke order matters: top to bottom, left to right.

example.roman: Wǒ huì xiě yì bǎi ge hànzì.
example.en: I can write a hundred characters.

note: Speech radical 讠, simplified from 讀: reading was reading aloud. 读书 'read books' also means 'to study, be at school'. Silent reading is 看书 'look at a book'.
Learned ability: 我会说中文 'I can speak Chinese'. Physical possibility is 能, permission 可以. Also 'will' for likely future (明天会下雨) and 'meeting' as a noun (开会). Simplified from 會.
演 'perform' (water radical, originally 'flow, develop') + 员 'member'. Gender is added only when needed: 女演员 actress, 男演员 actor. 电影演员 film actor. Measure word: 个 / 位 / 名.
Heart radical 忄 + 亡 'perish': the heart worn out. 你忙吗？ 'are you busy?'. 帮忙 (bāngmáng) is 'to help out'. 忙死了 'dead busy'.
作 'to make, do' + 业 'occupation, task' (simplified from 業). 做作业 'do homework' uses 做 and 作 side by side, both zuò. Chinese pupils get famously large amounts of it.
气 'air, breath, energy' is simplified from 氣 (rice 米 steaming). 天气怎么样？ 'how's the weather?'. 天气预报 the forecast. 气 is also the qi of 气功 qigong and 生气 'get angry'.
雨 is a pictograph of drops under a cloud and the radical of 雪, 雷, 雾. Rain 'comes down': 下雨了 'it's raining'. 雨伞 umbrella, 雨季 rainy season.
雪 is rain 雨 over a hand 彐 (sweeping). Follows the 下 pattern of 下雨. 雪花 snowflake, 雪人 snowman. Harbin's ice festival is the great 雪 event.
刮 'to scrape' (knife radical 刂): the wind scrapes past. 风 (from 風) is wind; 风水 'wind-water' feng shui, 风景 scenery. 今天刮大风 'it's very windy today'.
阳 is the yang of yin-yang: the sunny side of a hill (阝 hill + 日 sun). 月亮 the moon is its yin partner. 日 alone is the written 'sun/day' and never used in speech for the sun.
The spoken word for the moon in the sky; 月 alone means 'month'. 中秋节, the Mid-Autumn Festival, is the moon's night: families eat 月饼 and admire the full moon.
星 is the sun 日 over 生: 'born of light'. Doubling makes it the cosy everyday word; 星 alone is the celestial body and a celebrity 明星 'bright star'. Measure word: 颗.
Fire radical 灬 under 执. 今天很热 'it's hot today'. Also 'popular': 热门 a hot topic, 热情 warm-hearted, 热闹 lively and bustling, a quality Chinese love in a place.
Ice radical 冫 + 令. 天气很冷 'the weather is cold'. 冷水 cold water, 冷静 calm ('cold-quiet'). A 冷笑话 'cold joke' is a joke so bad it makes you shiver.
暖 has the sun radical 日; 和 is toneless here and read huo. Used for weather and rooms: 房间很暖和. 温暖 (wēnnuǎn) is 'warm' in the emotional sense.
凉 (ice radical 冫) is 'cool' as a good thing, unlike 冷. 凉快 describes a breezy evening; 凉水 is cool water, 凉菜 cold dishes. 'Chill out' is 凉快凉快.
春 shows plants sprouting under the sun 日. Seasons add 天: 春天, 夏天, 秋天, 冬天. 春节 the Spring Festival marks the start of spring on the lunar calendar.
夏 is also the name of the legendary first dynasty, the Xia. 夏天很热 'summer is hot'. 'Summer holiday' is 暑假 (shǔjià, 'heat holiday').
秋 is grain 禾 beside fire 火: the harvest season when stubble is burned. 中秋节 the Mid-Autumn Festival. Beijing's autumn is its best season: 秋高气爽 'autumn sky high, air crisp'.
冬 ends with the ice radical 冫 (two strokes at the bottom). 冬天很冷. Winter holiday is 寒假 'cold holiday'. 冬 gives its sound to 疼 'ache'.
A pictograph of three peaks. Measure word: 座. 爬山 'climb a mountain' is a favourite weekend activity. 山东 'east of the mountains', 山西 'west' are provinces. 火山 'fire mountain' is a volcano.
Water radical 氵 + 可. Measure word: 条. Originally the name of the Yellow River 黄河; 江 (as in 长江, the Yangtze) is the southern word. 河南 / 河北 provinces lie south / north of the river.
Water radical 氵 + 每. 上海 Shanghai 'on the sea', 海南 Hainan 'south of the sea'. 海鲜 'sea fresh' is seafood, 海外 'overseas'. 人山人海 'people mountain people sea' = a huge crowd.
Tree radical 木 (a pictograph of trunk and branches) + 对 + 寸; simplified from 樹. Measure word: 棵. Two 木 make 林 'woods', three make 森 'forest': 森林.
Grass radical 艹 + 化 'change'. Measure word: 朵 (a bloom) or 束 (a bouquet). The same character is the verb 'to spend' (花钱). 花园 garden, 烟花 fireworks ('smoke flowers').
Simplified from 雲 (rain radical 雨 over 云); the simple form 云 is the original pictograph of a curling cloud. 多云 'cloudy' in forecasts. 云南 Yunnan is 'south of the clouds'. Also 'cloud' computing: 云计算.
English 'typhoon' is thought to blend Chinese 大风 / 台风 (Cantonese 'tai fung') with Greek-Arabic 'tufan'. 台 is used for its sound. Typhoons hit the south-east coast every summer.
Rain radical 雨 over 务; simplified from 霧. 雾霾 (wùmái, 'fog-haze') is smog, a word every Beijinger knows. 有雾 'it's foggy'.
Animal radical 犭 (a squashed 犬 'dog') + 句. Measure word: 只 or 条. 热狗 'hot dog' is a direct translation. The Year of the Dog is one of the twelve zodiac years.

example.roman: Wǒ jiā yǒu yì zhī gǒu.
example.en: We have a dog at home.

note: Animal radical 犭 + 苗 'sprout', chosen for the sound; the cat's miao is the same across languages. Measure word: 只. 熊猫 'bear cat' is the panda. 猫 is also a 'modem' in tech slang (sound-loan).
Simplified from 買 (a net over 贝 'cowrie shell', the ancient money). 买 'buy' (third tone) and 卖 'sell' (fourth tone, with a 十 on top) are a notorious minimal pair. 买东西 'go shopping'.

example.roman: Wǒ mǎi le yì běn shū.

note: 买 with 十 on top: 'buy out', sell. Fourth tone, falling. 卖完了 'sold out'. 买卖 'buy-sell' is business. 外卖 'sell outside' is takeaway food.
Metal radical 钅: coins were bronze. Simplified from 錢. 多少钱？ 'how much?', 有钱 'rich', 钱包 wallet. Measure word: 笔 (a sum). 钱 is also a common surname.
Earth radical 土: a clod. The spoken unit of money, like 'buck': 十块钱 ten yuan. In writing and on price tags 元 is used. Also counts pieces: 一块蛋糕 a slice of cake.
The formal unit of 人民币 (rénmínbì, 'people's currency', RMB). Originally 圆 'round', after the round silver dollar; Japanese yen 円 and Korean won are the same word. 1 元 = 10 角 = 100 分.
A tenth of a yuan: 五毛 50 fen. Written 角 (jiǎo) on price tags. Also 'hair, fur, wool' and the surname of Mao Zedong, whose face is on every banknote.
多少 'how much / how many' is the pair 'many-few'. For small numbers 几 is used instead: 几块钱. Bargaining is still expected in markets, not in shops or supermarkets.
Shell radical 贝 at the bottom marks money words (买, 货, 费, 账), from cowrie shells used as currency. 太贵了！ 'too expensive!' is the bargaining opener. Also 'honoured': 贵姓 'your honourable surname'.

example.roman: Tài guì le, piányi yìdiǎn ba.
example.en: Too expensive, make it a bit cheaper.

note: 便 is read pián here but biàn 'convenient' in 方便 and 便利店 convenience store: a two-reading character. 占便宜 'take advantage'. 很便宜 'very cheap'.
商 'commerce' is also the Shang dynasty; the Shang people traded so widely that their name became the word for merchants. 店 'shop' (shelter radical 广): 书店 bookshop, 饭店 hotel. Measure word: 家.
Short for 超级市场 'super-level market', a direct translation. 超 'exceed' (walk radical 走) also gives 超人 Superman and slang 超好 'super good'. Measure word: 家.
市 'market, city' + 场 'open ground'. 菜市场 a food market, 市场经济 the market economy. 市 alone names cities: 北京市 Beijing Municipality. 夜市 is the night market.
Said to come from the East and West Markets of the Tang capital, where you went to buy things. 买东西 'buy things', 吃东西 'eat something'. With tone (dōngxī) it means the compass points.
逛 'to stroll' (walk radical 辶 + 狂 'wild'). Window-shopping and wandering a shopping street; 买东西 is shopping with a purpose. 逛商场 'wander the mall'.
付 is a hand 寸 beside a person 亻: handing something over. 付款 is the formal 'make payment' on screens; 支付 'pay' gives 支付宝 Alipay. Verb-object: 付了钱.
花 'flower' doubles as the verb 'to spend', for money and time (花时间). Verb-object: 花了很多钱 'spent a lot of money'. 乱花钱 is to squander.

example.roman: Tā huā le hěn duō qián mǎi chē.
example.en: He spent a lot of money on a car.

note: Discounts are stated as what you pay: 八折 'eight-tenths' = 20% off, 五折 = half price. 打折吗？ 'is there a discount?'. 折 'fold, snap' has the hand radical 扌.
一点 'a little' after an adjective means 'a bit more X': 快一点 quicker, 大一点 bigger. Add 儿 in Beijing: 一点儿 yìdiǎnr. The bargaining formula in any market.
信用 'credit, trustworthiness' + 卡, a sound-loan for 'card' (also 卡车 truck, from 'car'). Measure word: 张. Cards are rarer than phone payment in China; many shops take only 微信 or 支付宝.
'Money right here'. Cash has nearly vanished from Chinese cities; shops must by law still accept it. 现金 can be paid with 付现金. ATM is 取款机 'withdraw-money machine'.
扫 'sweep' + 码 'code' (stone radical 石, originally a weight). 二维码 'two-dimensional code' is the QR code. Every shop, menu and beggar's bowl has one: 扫码支付 'scan to pay'.

example.en: Can I pay by scanning the code?

note: An official tax receipt, printed by the tax authority; businesses need it for expenses, so 要发票吗？ 'do you want a fapiao?' follows every purchase. An ordinary till slip is 小票.
免 'exempt, avoid' (as in 免签 visa-free) + 费 'fee' (shell radical 贝). 免费 Wi-Fi is the two words you will search for most. 收费 is the opposite, 'charges apply'.
行 is read háng 'firm, row' here, not xíng 'go': 中国银行 Bank of China. The name recalls the silver-ingot economy of imperial China. Measure word: 家. 银行卡 bank card.
Cash in a red envelope, given at New Year by elders to children and at weddings. Measure word: 个. Since 2014 WeChat lets people send digital 红包; billions are sent each New Year's Eve.
高 'high' is a drawing of a tall tower; 兴 (from 興) is 'rise, mood', read xìng here but xīng when it means 'to flourish'. 我很高兴 'I am glad': adjectives take 很 and no 'to be'.

example.en: I'm very glad to meet you.

note: 'With the heart opened up'. The everyday word for feeling happy: 玩得很开心 'had a great time'. Its opposite 不开心 is the usual 'upset'. 心 is the radical of most feeling words.
快 'fast' has the heart radical 忄 and once meant 'pleased'. 乐 is lè 'joy' here, yuè 'music' in 音乐. The word for wishes: 生日快乐, 新年快乐, 圣诞快乐.
喜 is a drum 壴 over a mouth 口: music and song, joy. 喜欢 takes nouns or verbs: 我喜欢茶, 我喜欢看书. 'Love' for people is 爱; 喜欢 is 'have a crush on'.
Traditional 愛 has a heart 心 in the middle; the simplified 爱 replaced it with 友 'friend', which critics call 'love without a heart'. 我爱你 is said far less than in English; 爱人 was 'spouse'.
'To produce qi', the breath-energy rising. 别生气 'don't be angry', 他生我的气 'he's angry with me'. 气 also forms 客气 polite, 天气 weather, 空气 air.
Time that is hard to get through. 难 is nán 'difficult' here (nàn in 灾难 disaster). 伤心 'wounded heart' is sadder still. 我很难过 'I'm very sad'.
担 'to carry on a shoulder pole' (hand radical 扌): the heart as a burden. 别担心 'don't worry'. Its relief is 放心 'put the heart down'.
怕 is the heart radical 忄 beside 白 'white', a pale face. 我怕狗 'I'm afraid of dogs' uses 怕 alone with an object; 害怕 stands by itself. 可怕 is 'scary'.
紧 'tight' (silk radical) + 张 'stretch' (a drawn bow). Also 'in short supply': 时间很紧张 'time is tight'. 别紧张 'relax'.
无 'without' (from 無) + 聊 'to chat'. Nothing to talk about: both 'I'm bored' and 'this is boring'. 聊天 'chat the sky' = to chat. 无聊 is also 'silly, pointless'.
意思 'meaning' is one of the most flexible words: 有意思 interesting, 没意思 dull, 不好意思 embarrassed, 小意思 'a small token' said of a gift. 很有意思！ 'how interesting!'.

example.roman: Zhè běn shū hěn yǒu yìsi.

note: Two mouths 口口 (or eyes) over 犬 'dog': a howling. 别哭 'don't cry', 哭了 'burst into tears'. The crying emoji face is 哭脸.
Bamboo radical ⺮ over 夭 'bending': bamboo swaying like a laughing person, says one old explanation. One word for laugh and smile: 微笑 'tiny laugh' is a smile. 笑话 a joke. 哈哈 = haha.
舒 'stretch out, relax'. 很舒服 'very comfortable'; 不舒服 is the standard way to say you feel unwell: 我今天不太舒服. 舒 is also a surname.
讨 (speech radical 讠) 'to demand, provoke' + 厌 'to be sick of'. 我讨厌下雨 'I hate rain'. Said playfully, 讨厌！ is 'oh, you!'.
福 (altar radical 礻 + a wine jar) is the 'good fortune' character pasted upside down on doors at New Year, because 倒 'upside down' sounds like 到 'arrive'. 幸福 is happiness as a state of life.
To set your heart down and relax. 放心吧 'don't worry about it', 我不放心 'I'm uneasy'. 放 'to put, release' also gives 放假 'release a holiday' = be on holiday.

example.roman: Fàngxīn ba, wǒ huì bāng nǐ.

note: 'Lovable', the same two characters as Japanese kawaii 可愛い. 可 + verb = '-able': 可怕 scary, 可笑 laughable, 可能 possible. Much used for babies, pandas and cartoon stickers.
感 is 咸 over a heart 心; 觉 is jué 'perceive' here (jiào in 睡觉 'sleep'). 我感觉很累 'I feel tired'. 觉得 (juéde) 'to think, feel that' is its sibling.
'To eat a fright'; 吃 'eat' is used for taking things in: 吃苦 'eat bitterness' = endure hardship, 吃亏 'eat loss' = get the worse of it. 惊 has the heart radical 忄 (simplified from 驚, a startled horse).
满 'full' (water radical 氵) + 意 'wish': the wish is filled. 你满意吗？ 'are you satisfied?'. 满 also means 'Manchu' (满族), the people of the Qing dynasty.
太 ... 了 wraps an adjective to mean 'extremely': 太贵了 too expensive, 太棒了 awesome, 太谢谢你了 thank you so much. 太 is 大 'big' with an extra dot: 'bigger than big'.
糟 'wine dregs, a mess' + 糕 'cake' (both rice radical 米). 糟糕！ is 'damn, oh no!', and 糟糕的天气 'terrible weather'. 糟了！ on its own means 'uh-oh'.

example.roman: Zāogāo, wǒ wàng le dài qiánbāo.
example.en: Oh no, I forgot to bring my wallet.

note: Both characters have 心 'heart' at the bottom. 我很想念你 'I miss you a lot'; in conversation just 我想你. 念 alone is 'to read aloud, to think of'.
Mouth radical 口 + 乞 'beg'. 吃饭 'eat rice' = have a meal, and 你吃了吗？ 'have you eaten?' is a classic greeting. Also for medicine (吃药) and hardship (吃苦).

example.roman: Nǐ chī guo Běijīng kǎoyā ma?
example.en: Have you ever eaten Peking duck?

note: Mouth radical 口 + 曷. 喝水, 喝茶, 喝酒. Soup is drunk, not eaten: 喝汤. 喝多了 'drank too much'. Read hè, the same character means 'to shout': 喝彩 'cheer'.
去 + place: 去中国, 去学校. 去 + verb = 'go and do': 去吃饭 'go eat'. After another verb it marks direction away from the speaker: 出去 go out, 回去 go back. The opposite is 来.

example.en: Have you been to the Great Wall?

note: Simplified from 來, originally a picture of a wheat plant, borrowed for the sound. Direction towards the speaker: 进来 come in, 回来 come back. 来一个 'bring one' orders food; 来了！ 'coming!'.

en: to look, to watch, to read
note: A hand 手 shading an eye 目, peering into the distance. 看书 read, 看电视 watch TV, 看医生 see a doctor, 看朋友 visit a friend. 看看 / 看一下 'take a look'. 好看 'good-looking'.
Simplified 听 is a mouth 口 and 斤; traditional 聽 had an ear 耳, an eye and a heart 心: listening with all three. 听音乐 listen to music, 好听 'nice to hear', 听说 'hear say' = I've heard that.
Speech radical 讠 + 兑. 说中文 'speak Chinese', 说话 'talk', 听说 'I hear that'. Simplified from 說. 说 after a verb reports speech: 他说他很忙 'he says he's busy', no 'that' needed.

example.en: Please speak a bit more slowly.

note: Person radical 亻 + 故. 做饭 cook, 做作业 do homework, 做朋友 'be friends'. 你做什么工作？ 'what do you do?'. Same sound as 坐 sit and 作, so context decides.
A hand holding meat 月. Negated with 没, never 不: 没有 'don't have'. Also 'there is': 这儿有银行吗？ 'is there a bank here?'. 有 + 没有 makes a question: 你有没有时间？

en: to want to; to think; to miss
note: 相 'look at' over a heart 心. Three jobs: 想 + verb 'would like to' (我想去), 想 + clause 'think' (我想他不来), 想 + person 'miss' (我想你). 想一想 'think it over'.

example.en: I'd like to go to Shanghai.

note: A woman 女 with hands on her hips (originally 'waist', now 腰). 我要水 'I want water'; 要 + verb 'am going to / must': 我要走了 'I'm leaving'. 不要 is 'don't want' or 'don't!'; 'needn't' is 不用.
知 is an arrow 矢 and a mouth 口: speaking straight to the point. 道 'way, Dao' is toneless here. 不知道 'I don't know' is heard constantly. Knowing a person is 认识, not 知道.

example.roman: Wǒ bù zhīdào tā shì shéi.
example.en: I don't know who he is.

note: Silk radical 纟 + 合; simplified from 給. Two objects, like English: 给我一杯茶 'give me a cup of tea'. Also 'for, to': 给你打电话 'call you'. 给 is read jǐ in 供给 'supply'.
Hand radical 扌 + 戈 'spear'. 找 is the searching; 找到 'find' adds the result 到. 找工作 job-hunt, 找人 look for someone. Also 'give change': 找你十块 'here's ten yuan change'.

example.roman: Wǒ zài zhǎo wǒ de shǒujī.

note: Bamboo radical ⺮ over 寺 'temple'. 等一下 / 等等 'wait a moment', 等人 wait for someone. Also 'etc.' at the end of a list, and 'grade': 一等 first class.
帮 has the cloth radical 巾 under 邦 'state'. In speech 帮 alone is commoner: 帮我一下 'give me a hand', 帮忙 'help out'. 帮助 is the fuller verb and noun: 谢谢你的帮助.
电话 'electric speech' is the telephone; 打 'hit' is the verb for making a call. 给我打电话 'call me'. A video call is 视频电话, voice messages on WeChat 语音.
Jade radical 王 + 元: playing with a jade trinket. Covers any leisure: 玩游戏 play games, 出去玩 go out and have fun, 去北京玩 visit Beijing for fun. 好玩 'fun'. Often 玩儿 in Beijing.
A figure with swinging arms over a foot 止: originally 'run'. Now 'walk' and 'leave': 我走了 'I'm off', 走吧 'let's go'. Add 路 for 'go on foot'. 走 is the radical of 起, 超, 越.

example.roman: Shíjiān bù zǎo le, wǒmen zǒu ba.

note: A spiral: something circling back. 回家 go home, 回国 return to one's country, 回来 come back, 回去 go back. 回答 'answer', 回信 'reply to a letter'. Also counts occasions: 一回 once.
Simplified from 開: two hands lifting the bar of a gate. 开门 open the door, 开灯 switch on, 开会 hold a meeting, 开始 begin, 开玩笑 joke. The all-purpose 'start, open, operate' verb.
Simplified from 關, a bar across a gate 門. 关门 close the door, 关灯 switch off, 关机 turn off the phone. 关系 'connection, relationship' and 没关系 'never mind' grow from the same root.
Both characters have the speech radical 讠. For people and places: 我认识他 'I know him'; 你认识这个字吗？ 'do you know this character?'. Facts take 知道. 很高兴认识你 'nice to meet you'.
A mouth 口 in a doorway 门: asking at the gate. 问问题 'ask a question', 请问 'may I ask', 问路 'ask the way'. Not for requests: 'ask someone to do' is 请 or 让.

example.roman: Wǒ xiǎng wèn yí ge wèntí.
example.en: I'd like to ask a question.

note: 告 is an ox 牛 over a mouth 口; 诉 (speech radical 讠) is toneless here. Takes two objects: 告诉我你的名字 'tell me your name'. 'Tell a story' is 讲故事, not 告诉.
Originally a drawing of a toothed weapon, borrowed for the sound. No case: 我 is I and me. Plural adds 们: 我们 we. 我的 'my'. Spoken Chinese often drops it when the subject is obvious.
Person radical 亻 + 尔, an old form of 'you'. 你们 you (plural), 你的 your. Polite 您 adds a heart below. 你好 'hello' is simply 'you good'.
Simplified from 這 (walk radical 辶 + 言); the simplified form uses 文. 这个 'this one' (often zhèige in speech), 这儿 / 这里 'here', 这些 'these', 这样 'like this'.
那个 'that one', 那儿 / 那里 'there', 那些 those. Also 'then, in that case' at the start of a sentence: 那我们走吧 'then let's go'. Differs from 哪 'which' only by the mouth 口 and tone.
Question words stay where the answer would go: 你叫什么？ 'you are called what?'. 什么 + noun = 'which': 什么时候 when, 什么地方 where. 没什么 'it's nothing'.
Speech radical 讠 + 隹 (a bird). Both shéi and shuí are accepted readings; shéi is what you hear. 他是谁？ 'who is he?', 谁的 'whose'. Simplified from 誰.
哪 'which' + the Beijing 儿 ending; the south says 哪里 (nǎlǐ). 你去哪儿？ 'where are you going?' is a common greeting. 哪里哪里 is a modest 'oh, not at all' to a compliment.
为 'for the sake of' + 什么 'what'. The answer uses 因为 'because'. 为 is read wèi here and in 因为; wéi in 成为 'become'.
怎么 + verb: 怎么走？ 'how do I get there?', 怎么说 'how do you say'. 怎么样 is 'how about / how is it': 天气怎么样？. 怎么了？ 'what's wrong?'.

example.en: How do you read this character?

note: Simplified from 幾. Asks for numbers under about ten, with a measure word: 几个人 how many people, 几点 what time, 几岁 how old (a child). Also 'a few': 几个朋友.
For any size of number and without a measure word: 多少钱 how much money, 多少人 how many people. Also asks for numbers themselves: 你的电话是多少？ 'what's your number?'.
时候 'the time when' (候 toneless). 你什么时候来？ 'when are you coming?'. For clock time use 几点. The answer slot is the same: 我明天来.
Mouth radical 口 + 马 'horse', toneless. Turns any statement into a yes/no question: 你是老师吗？ Never used with question words (什么, 谁) or with the 'verb-not-verb' question (是不是).
Bounces a question back: 我很好，你呢？ 'I'm fine, and you?'. Also asks 'where is': 我的书呢？ 'where's my book?'. And marks something ongoing: 他在睡觉呢 'he's sleeping'.
The most frequent character in Chinese. Links a modifier to a noun: 我的书 my book, 红色的车 a red car, 我买的东西 'the things I bought'. Dropped between close pairs: 我妈妈 my mum.
Two jobs: after a verb, an action completed (我吃了 I ate); at the end of a sentence, a new situation (下雨了 it's started raining, 我饿了 I've got hungry). Not simply 'past tense'. Read liǎo in 了解.
A bird flying up to the sky and not coming down, by one old account. Fourth tone, but second before another fourth tone: 不是 bú shì, 不对 bú duì. 不 negates most verbs; 有 takes 没.
Negates 有 and past actions: 我没有钱 'I have no money', 我没去 'I didn't go'. Often shortened to 没. 没有 as a one-word reply means 'no, I haven't / there isn't'.
Step radical 彳 + 艮. Placed before an adjective almost automatically: 我很好 'I'm fine', where 很 carries little meaning. Without it, 我好 sounds like a comparison is coming. 非常 is a real 'very'.
Goes before the verb, never at the end: 我也是 'me too', 我也去 'I'm going too'. 也 + 不 = 'neither': 我也不喜欢. Often paired with 都: 也都.
Sums up whatever comes before it: 我们都是学生 'we are all students', 什么都 'anything at all'. Read dū it means 'capital city': 首都 the capital, 成都 Chengdu.
Joins nouns only: 我和你 'you and I', 茶和咖啡. Clauses are simply put side by side, no 'and'. 和 also means 'harmony, peace': 和平 peace, 和谐 harmony. 跟 (gēn) is a spoken synonym.
Often paired with 虽然 'although' in the first clause: 虽然贵，但是很好 'expensive, but good'. 可是 (kěshì) and bare 但 are softer variants. 不过 'however' is the most casual.

example.roman: Wǒ xiǎng qù, dànshì méiyǒu shíjiān.
example.en: I'd like to go, but I don't have time.

note: Mouth radical 口 + 巴, toneless. Softens into a suggestion or agreement: 走吧 'let's go', 好吧 'okay then'. After a statement it asks for confirmation: 你是老师吧？ 'you're a teacher, right?'.
Chinese has no single 'yes': you repeat the verb or say 对 'correct'. 对不对？ 'right?', 不对 'wrong'. Also 'towards, to': 对我说 'said to me', and 'pair' (一对). 对不起 'sorry' is 'cannot face you'.
A person with arms stretched wide. 大学 university, 大人 adult, 大家 everyone, 大夫 doctor (dàifu). 多大？ 'how old?' asks 'how big'. Opposite: 小.
Three small strokes, grains of sand. 小心 careful, 小时 hour, 小姐 miss, 小学 primary school. 小 + surname is a friendly address for a younger person: 小王 'young Wang'.
Two pieces of meat 夕 stacked: plenty. 很多 'a lot', 多少 how much, 多 + adjective asks degree: 多大 how old, 多长 how long. 多谢 'many thanks'.

example.en: Beijing has a lot of people.

note: 小 with a stroke cut away: less. 很少 'very few / rarely', 少一点 'a bit less'. Read shào it means 'young': 少年 youth, 少林 Shaolin ('young forest' temple).
A woman 女 with a child 子. Also 'very' (好久 a long time), 'easy to' (好吃 tasty, 好看 pretty), and 'okay' as a reply: 好的, 好吧. Read hào it means 'to be fond of' (爱好 hobby).
Earth radical 土 + 不; simplified from 壞. 坏人 bad person, 坏了 'it's broken' (phone, fridge, plan). 坏蛋 'bad egg' = scoundrel. Food that has gone off is 坏了 too.
An axe 斤 cutting fresh wood 木: newly cut. 新年 new year, 新闻 'new hearing' = news, 新鲜 fresh. 新加坡 Singapore and 新疆 'new frontier' both begin with it.
For objects and the past: 旧衣服 old clothes, 旧书 second-hand books. People are 老, never 旧. Simplified from 舊 (an owl on a nest). 新旧 'new and old'.
Heart radical 忄 + 夬; originally 'pleased' (快乐). 快一点 'faster', 快车 express. 快 + verb + 了 means 'about to': 快下雨了 'it's about to rain'. Homophone of 块 'yuan' and 筷 chopsticks.

example.en: The high-speed train is very fast.

note: Heart radical 忄 + 曼. 慢一点 'slower', 慢慢来 'take your time', 慢走 'go carefully' said to a departing guest, 慢用 'enjoy your meal'.
Originally an old man with long hair. 长城 the Great Wall ('long wall'), 长江 the Yangtze ('long river'). Read zhǎng it means 'grow' or 'chief': 长大 grow up, 校长 head teacher.
A tall building with a tower on top. 他很高 'he's tall', 高铁 high-speed rail, 高兴 happy, 高考 the university entrance exam. 高 is also a common surname.
Arrow radical 矢 + 委. For people and buildings only; a short length or time is 短 (duǎn). 他比我矮 'he is shorter than me'.
漂 'to float' (water radical) + 亮 'bright', toneless. For people, clothes, cities and a job well done: 做得漂亮 'nicely done'. 美 (sheep 羊 + big 大, a fat sheep) is 'beautiful' in a loftier sense.
Pattern 好 + verb: 好看 nice to look at, 好听 nice to hear, 好吃 nice to eat, 好玩 fun. 不好看 is the gentle way to say something is ugly; 难看 'hard to look at' is blunter.
Simplified from 難 (a bird 隹 on the right). 中文很难吗？ 'is Chinese hard?'. 难 + verb = 'hard to': 难看 ugly, 难吃 disgusting, 难过 sad. Read nàn: 'disaster' (灾难).
容 'to contain, allow' + 易 'easy, change' (the 易 of 易经 I Ching). 很容易 'very easy'; 容易 + verb = 'prone to': 容易生病 'gets sick easily'. 不容易 is high praise for effort.
重 is zhòng 'heavy' here, chóng 'again' in 重复. 很重要 'very important', 最重要的是 'the most important thing is'. 重点 'heavy point' = key point.
'Having a name'. 很有名 'very famous'; 名 'name' is a mouth 口 under the evening 夕, calling out a name in the dark. 著名 is the formal 'renowned', 名人 a celebrity.
干 'dry' (from 乾) + 净 'clean' (ice radical 冫). 很干净 'very clean'. 吃干净 'eat it all up'. Note 干 is also gàn 'to do' (干什么？ 'what are you doing?'), a two-reading character.
Flesh radical 月 + 庄. Simplified 脏 stands for two traditional characters: 髒 'dirty' (zāng) and 臟 'internal organ' (zàng, as in 心脏 heart). 脏话 is swearing, 'dirty talk'.
聪 has the ear radical 耳 (keen hearing) and 明 is sun + moon (clear sight): a clever person hears and sees well. 明 is toneless here. 小聪明 'petty cleverness' is a mild insult.
'Light in years'. 轻 'light in weight' (vehicle radical 车). 年轻人 young people. 小 can also mean young: 他比我小 'he is younger than me'.
An old person with long hair and a stick. For people and as a mark of respect: 老师 teacher, 老板 boss, 老王 'old Wang' (friendly), 老外 'old foreigner' (a nickname for Westerners). Things are 旧.
Flesh radical 月 + 半. 胖子 'fatty' is said far more freely than in English, though it is getting less polite. Opposite 瘦 (shòu, thin, with the sickness radical 疒). 胖胖的 'chubby' is affectionate.
城 'city wall' (earth radical 土 + 成) + 市 'market': a walled town with a market. Measure word: 座 or 个. 城里 'in town'. The old 城 of Beijing was torn down in the 1950s.
京 'capital' is a tower on a hill. Named in 1403 when the Ming moved the court north from 南京 'southern capital'. 'Peking' is an older romanisation; Peking duck and Peking University keep it.
上 'on, above' + 海 'sea'. China's largest city; its dialect 上海话 is unintelligible to Mandarin speakers. The local word for self is 阿拉. Locals call it 魔都, the 'magic capital'.

中 'middle' + 国 'country' (a frame 囗 around 玉 jade; traditional 國 held 或, a spear guarding land). 中国人 Chinese person, 中国菜 Chinese food. 'China' in English is usually traced to the Qin 秦 dynasty, via Sanskrit.

example.en: I'm going to China next year.

note: 地 'earth, ground' + 方 'direction' (toneless). 什么地方？ 'what place?', 好地方 'a nice spot'. 地方 with full tones (dìfāng) means 'local' as opposed to central: 地方政府 local government.
园 'garden' is simplified from 園 (a frame 囗 around 袁). Measure word: 个 / 座. Chinese parks are social hubs: morning tai chi, square dancing, matchmaking corners. 动物园 is the zoo.

example.roman: Zǎoshang gōngyuán li yǒu hěn duō rén.
example.en: There are lots of people in the park in the morning.

note: Measure word: 家 / 个. Malls in China are huge, with food courts on the top floor. 逛商场 'wander the mall'. 购物中心 'purchase centre' is the formal term.
图书 'illustrated books' is the formal word for books as a collection. 馆 'establishment' (food radical 饣, originally an inn): 博物馆 museum, 大使馆 embassy. Measure word: 个 / 座.
电影 'electric shadow' is a film, after the shadow-puppet theatre 皮影. 院 'courtyard, institution' (hill radical 阝). 看电影 'see a film'. Measure word: 家.
博 'broad, learned' (as in 博士 PhD) + 物 'things' + 馆. Measure word: 家 / 座. The 故宫博物院 'Palace Museum' is the Forbidden City; most state museums are free with ID.
店 'shop' pattern: 书店 bookshop, 花店 florist, 饭店 hotel/restaurant, 便利店 convenience store. 新华书店 Xinhua is the state chain found in every town. Measure word: 家.
Also 药房 'medicine room'. Chinese pharmacies sell both 西药 Western drugs and 中药 herbal medicine, often over the counter. Measure word: 家. Look for the green cross sign.
邮 (city radical 阝) 'post', also 邮件 mail, 电子邮件 e-mail, 邮箱 mailbox. 局 'bureau, office' for public services: 警察局 police station. China Post's colour is green.
警 has 言 'speech' under 敬 'respect'; 察 'to examine'. 警察局 police station. 公安 'public security' is the official name of the force; 110 is the emergency number.
广 'broad' is the simplified form of 廣, reduced to its roof. 天安门广场 Tiananmen Square is the famous one. 广场舞 'square dancing' is the evening exercise of retired women everywhere.
Tree radical 木 + 乔 'tall'; simplified from 橋. Measure word: 座. 天桥 'sky bridge' is a pedestrian overpass. 桥 is also a surname; Qiao in English.
Simply 'the long wall'; the full name 万里长城 is the 'ten-thousand-li long wall'. Mao's line 不到长城非好汉 'you're no hero until you've reached the Great Wall' is on every souvenir.
The narrow lanes of old Beijing, lined with courtyard houses 四合院. The word is usually traced to Mongolian 'hottog' (water well), from the Yuan dynasty. Measure word: 条.
寺 is a Buddhist temple (少林寺 Shaolin), 庙 a shrine to gods or ancestors (孔庙 Confucius temple). 庙会 'temple fairs' are New Year markets. Measure word: 座.
农 'agriculture' (from 農) + 村 'village' (tree radical 木). 农民 farmer, 农历 the lunar 'farmers' calendar'. The 城市 / 农村 divide, with its 户口 residence permits, shapes Chinese life.
'State and family' together: Confucian thought saw the state as the family writ large. 国 is the 国 of 中国, 美国 (USA, 'beautiful country'), 英国, 法国 ('law country', France).
A Buddhist coinage translating Sanskrit lokadhātu: 世 'age' + 界 'realm'. 全世界 'the whole world', 世界杯 the World Cup. 世 shows three tens 十: thirty years, a generation.
外国人 is 'foreigner' (polite); 老外 'old outsider' is the colloquial nickname. 出国 'go abroad', 外语 foreign language, 外交 'outside relations' = diplomacy.
Measure word: 家. Chengdu is famous for bamboo-chair teahouses where people play mahjong all afternoon. Lao She's play 《茶馆》 (1957) uses one to show fifty years of Beijing history.
中心 'centre' is literally 'middle heart': 购物中心 shopping centre, 中心 of anything. 去市中心怎么走？ 'how do I get downtown?'. 市区 'city district' is the urban area.
